title: Mesher: rebuild sub-cell surface height from column heights (remove stair ripples)
player_outcome: Gentle slopes are smooth ramps instead of rippling contour-line terraces every few metres. Walking, grass and placed objects follow a smooth ground.
design: Root cause, checked in code: SurfaceNetsMesher places each vertex at the edge-crossing centroid of binary occupancy. Taubin smoothing (8 iterations, λ 0.5 / μ -0.53, MaxDrift 0.45) acts as a low-pass filter that preserves low frequencies, so staircases with steps 6 or more cells long survive as ripples. Sub-cell height is lost at the pass-1 threshold (GlobalDensityPass.cs:36).

Add src/Strata.Core/Meshing/HeightfieldSmoothing.cs (internal static, ThreadStatic scratch). Make SurfaceNetsMesher.Scratch internal and call HeightfieldSmoothing.Apply(vol, scratch) right after Relax(). SurfaceNetsMesher.cs is 371 lines: add only the call.

For each Free dual vertex (x,y,z), first test it is up-facing and monotone: at least 2 of the bottom 4 corners opaque, at most 2 of the top 4 opaque, and no vertical corner pair with opaque above air.

Then gather columns cx ∈ [x+1-R, x+R], cz likewise (R = 4). For each column, find the top transition inside the local window [y-4, y+5]: opaque below, air above, solid under it within the window, no Snap (crisp or placed) cell in the window. That gives H = y'+1. Reject columns with |H - Hcentre| > 3 (cliffs). Require at least 75% valid columns.

S = tent-weighted mean of H with weight (R+0.5-|dx|)(R+0.5-|dz|). New y = clamp(S) to both the dual cell [y+0.52, y+1.48] and Initial ± MaxDrift (0.45). This keeps the ≤ 0.225 m deviation that FeetCell and IsStandable assume. x and z stay from Taubin; normals still come from the density field.

Chunk borders stay watertight because only a local window is read (±4 columns, ±5 cells from the dual cell), inside the 16-cell margin of both neighbouring neighbourhoods. Do not use a 'topmost surface in region' scan: it differs between vertically adjacent chunks and would crack horizontal borders.
Performance: cache column scans per (cx, cz, window base) in a ThreadStatic sbyte grid over the dual range. Budget: at most +1.5 ms median per chunk in mesh-bench.
MeshBenchCommand: add --roughness, printing the RMS deviation (cm) of up-facing vertex heights from a local 3×3-neighbour plane fit, for before/after evidence.
files_modify: src/Strata.Core/Meshing/SurfaceNetsMesher.cs — Scratch internal; call HeightfieldSmoothing after Relax
files_add: src/Strata.Core/Meshing/HeightfieldSmoothing.cs — sub-cell height reconstruction for up-facing smooth vertices
tests: GentleRampHasNoStairs: natural stone ramp rising 1 cell per 6 along X through chunk (1,1,1); up-facing vertices away from borders deviate from the ideal plane by less than 0.15 cells max, RMS < 0.06 (today about 0.3-0.5)
SteepRampStaysInDualCells: 45° ramp, no vertex leaves its dual cell or exceeds MaxDrift
HorizontalBorderMatches: like GeneratedTerrainBordersMatchBetweenChunks but between chunk a and a+(0,1,0); the existing X-border test still passes
Existing MeshingTests: single natural block not collapsed, crisp blocks exact, MeshingIsDeterministic
verification: dotnet run --project tools/Strata.Tools -- mesh-bench --seed=1234 --roughness before and after: roughness at least 50% lower, median ms ≤ +1.5
Smoke movement.cmds and basic.cmds (walking, player.on_floor); in game with F3 on rolling forest near spawn, look along slopes at low sun
risks: Thin roofs and ledges could be pulled down: the monotone-window and ±3 cliff rejection must hold
Colliders come from the same triangles, so ObjectPlacement.Ground and grass follow automatically; check trees and chests do not sink
